title: Disrupting DDB2-DNA Interaction by Lapatinib Enhances Chemotherapy Sensitivity.
authors: Hsu, Shih-Chao; He, Yu-Hao; Chen, Yun-Ju; Le, Uyen Nguyen Phuong; Liu, Pei-Tong; Huynh, Thanh Kieu; Chen, Yi-Ling; Wei, Ya-Ling; Chou, Hsin-Chiao; Huang, Wei-Chien; Jeng, Long-Bin
one_liner_zh: 该文通过虚拟筛选和分子动力学模拟发现拉帕替尼可破坏DDB2-DNA复合物，研究广义蛋白-DNA互作界面并用于化疗增敏，方法可迁移至TF-DNA体系。
abstract: Chemoresistance remains an obstacle to effective cancer therapy across multiple tumor types. Damaged DNA-binding protein 2 (DDB2), a key component of the nucleotide excision repair (NER) pathway, contributes to chemoresistance by enhancing DNA repair and inhibiting apoptosis. Although the role of DDB2 in tumor progression is context-dependent, its upregulation has been associated with poor prognosis in various malignancies. In this study, elevated DDB2 levels found in breast, liver, cholangiocarcinoma, and lung cancers correlated with reduced patient survival. DDB2 confers resistance to chemotherapeutic agents. Through structure-based virtual screening and molecular dynamics simulations, lapatinib, an FDA-approved EGFR/HER2 inhibitor, was identified as a compound capable of disrupting the DDB2/DNA complex, which was confirmed by the cellular thermal shift assay and chromatin fractionation. Mechanistically, lapatinib binds to the DNA-binding region of DDB2, thereby reducing its chromatin association and promoting proteasomal degradation. Co-treatment with lapatinib and doxorubicin exhibited synergistic cytotoxicity in both cancer cell lines and patient-derived organoids. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for lapatinib in targeting DNA repair machinery, supporting its repurposing as a chemosensitizing agent. Our study highlights DDB2 as a critical mediator of chemoresistance and proposes disruption of DDB2-dependent DNA repair as a novel strategy for chemosensitization.
abstract_zh: 化疗耐药性仍然是多种肿瘤类型有效癌症治疗中的障碍。损伤DNA结合蛋白2（DDB2）是核苷酸切除修复（NER）通路的关键组分，通过增强DNA修复和抑制凋亡而促进化疗耐药性。尽管DDB2在肿瘤进展中的作用具有情境依赖性，但其上调与多种恶性肿瘤的不良预后相关。在本研究中，乳腺癌、肝癌、胆管癌和肺癌中发现的DDB2水平升高与患者生存期缩短相关。DDB2赋予化疗药物耐药性。通过基于结构的虚拟筛选和分子动力学模拟，拉帕替尼（lapatinib），一种FDA批准的EGFR/HER2抑制剂，被鉴定为能够破坏DDB2/DNA复合物的化合物，这通过细胞热位移实验和染色质分级分离得到证实。机制上，拉帕替尼结合DDB2的DNA结合区域，从而减少其染色质关联并促进蛋白酶体降解。拉帕替尼与多柔比星联合治疗在癌细胞系和患者来源的类器官中表现出协同细胞毒性。这些发现揭示了拉帕替尼在靶向DNA修复机制中的先前未被认识的作用，支持其作为化疗增敏剂的再利用。我们的研究强调DDB2是化疗耐药性的关键介导因子，并提出破坏DDB2依赖性DNA修复作为化疗增敏的新策略。
